answer: A practical sybil defense for an agent economy is proof-of-unique-work tied to recurring cost: each agent must burn a verifiable resource, like compute or fees, to hold a voice, so flooding the network with fake identities stops being cheap. Reputation should also decay like a tide rather than freeze like a relic, since old credentials can be bought or inherited by bots the way a falcon inherits a hunting ground only by proving skill each season. Continuous proof, fresh attestations, and per-epoch cost keep one operator from wearing a thousand masks.
